provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Agriculture: why farming matters
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state reasons why farming matters.
The pupils should be able to list common farm tools.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about plants and animals. Today we will learn how farming helps us.

Content:
Farming gives us food like rice and beans. It also gives us crops to sell for naira. Farm tools help farmers work. Common tools include cutlass for clearing grass, hoe for digging, and rake for leveling soil. Our fathers use these tools on the farm.

Class activity:
Bring pictures of farm tools. Let pupils name each tool and show how to use it.

Evaluation questions:
Why is farming important?
Name three farm tools.
What crop do we eat in Nigeria?

Summary:
Farming gives us food and money. Farm tools help farmers do their work.

topics.title: Agriculture: plant a seed
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plant a maize seed correctly.
The pupils should be able to explain the care routine for a seedling.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about farm tools. Today we will plant maize seeds like farmers do.

Content:
Planting seeds is the first step in farming. We need soil, water, and maize seeds. First, fill a cup with soil. Make a small hole in the soil. Put one seed in the hole. Cover the seed lightly with soil. Water it gently. The seed needs water, sunlight, and care to grow.

Class activity:
Each pupil will plant a maize seed in a cup. They will water it daily and watch it grow.

Evaluation questions:
What do we need to plant a seed?
How deep should we plant the seed?
What does a seed need to grow?

Summary:
Planting seeds is easy with soil, water, and care. We must water our seeds daily.

topics.title: Home economics: my body
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper bathing routine.
The pupils should be able to list clean habits for good health.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about personal cleanliness. Today we will learn how to care for our bodies.

Content:
Keeping our bodies clean is very important. We bathe every morning with soap and water. We wash our face, hands, and feet. We also brush our teeth to keep them clean. Clean habits prevent sickness. When we are clean, people like to be near us.

Class activity:
Let pupils demonstrate how to wash hands properly. They will show each step: wet hands, apply soap, rub hands, rinse, and dry.

Evaluation questions:
Why is bathing important?
What should we use to brush our teeth?
Name two clean habits.

Summary:
Bathing daily keeps us healthy and clean. Good habits prevent germs.

topics.title: Home economics: the kitchen
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name common kitchen tools.
The pupils should be able to explain safe kitchen habits.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about bathing. Today we will learn about the kitchen where food is prepared.

Content:
The kitchen is where we cook food. Common kitchen tools include pot for cooking, spoon for stirring, and knife for cutting. We must be safe in the kitchen. We keep knives away from small children. We turn pot handles away from the stove to prevent accidents.

Class activity:
Bring pictures of kitchen tools. Let pupils name each tool and tell how to use it safely.

Evaluation questions:
Name three kitchen tools.
Why must pot handles face inward?
What should we avoid in the kitchen?

Summary:
Kitchen tools help us cook food. Safety in the kitchen prevents accidents.

topics.title: Agriculture: farm animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name common farm animals.
The pupils should be able to identify where farm animals live.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about plants. Today we will learn about animals that live on farms.

Content:
Farm animals are important to us. Cow gives us milk. Chicken gives us eggs. Goat gives us meat. These animals live in different homes. Cows live in sheds. Chickens live in coops. Goats live in pens. Each animal makes its own sound. Cows moo. Chickens cluck. Goats bleat.

Class activity:
Let pupils pretend to be farm animals. They will make the animal sounds and show how the animals move.

Evaluation questions:
Name three farm animals.
What does a chicken give us?
Where do cows live?

Summary:
Farm animals give us food. They live in special homes on the farm.

topics.title: Home economics: food groups
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify simple food groups.
The pupils should be able to arrange a healthy plate of food.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about farm animals. Today we will learn about the food groups that make us healthy.

Content:
Food is divided into groups. Carbohydrates give us energy. Examples include rice and yam. Proteins help us grow. Examples include beans and fish. Vegetables and fruits keep us strong. We should eat from all groups to stay healthy. A healthy plate has food from each group.

Class activity:
Let pupils draw a healthy plate. They will draw food from each food group on their plates.

Evaluation questions:
What do carbohydrates give us?
Name one protein food.
Why should we eat vegetables?

Summary:
Food groups help us stay healthy. We should eat from all groups every day.

topics.title: Agriculture: watering and weeding
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to water plants.
The pupils should be able to identify garden tools for weeding.

Introduction:
Last term we planted maize seeds. Today we will learn how to care for plants by watering and weeding.

Content:
Plants need water to grow. We water plants in the morning or evening. We use watering can to give water slowly. Weeds are unwanted plants that take food from our crops. We remove weeds with hand trowel or hoe. Weeding helps our plants grow well.

Class activity:
Let pupils water the class garden. They will also remove weeds using small garden tools.

Evaluation questions:
When should we water plants?
What are weeds?
Name two tools for weeding.

Summary:
Watering and weeding help plants grow strong. We must care for our plants daily.

topics.title: Home economics: washing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wash a handkerchief properly.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to dry and fold clothes.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about kitchen safety. Today we will learn how to wash and fold clothes.

Content:
Washing clothes keeps them clean. First, we soak the clothes in water. Then we apply soap and rub gently. We rinse until the water runs clear. After washing, we hang clothes to dry in the sun. When dry, we fold neatly and put away.

Class activity:
Each pupil will wash a small handkerchief. They will rinse, dry, and fold it properly.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to wash clothes?
Why do we dry clothes in the sun?
How should we fold clothes?

Summary:
Washing clothes makes them clean. Proper folding keeps clothes neat.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship: helping hands
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to suggest little jobs for little pay.
The pupils should be able to participate in a class job chart.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about helping at home. Today we will learn how to earn money by helping others.

Content:
We can earn money by doing small jobs. We can wash plates for neighbors. We can help carry goods in the market. We can sweep compound for a small fee. These jobs teach us responsibility. We also learn the value of hard work and money.

Class activity:
Create a class job chart. Pupils will choose jobs like cleaning黑板 or arranging books. They will do the jobs all week.

Evaluation questions:
Name one job we can do for money.
Why is working good for us?
What does hard work teach us?

Summary:
Small jobs help us earn money. Working teaches us responsibility.

topics.title: Revision and exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to display their garden cup.
The pupils should be able to explain what they learned this term.

Introduction:
This term we learned about farming, home economics, and entrepreneurship. Today we will show our work.

Content:
We will display our garden cups with growing maize plants. We will show the kitchen tools we learned about. We will demonstrate how to wash clothes and fold them neatly. We will also show our class job chart and explain the jobs we did.

Class activity:
Each pupil will bring their work to display. They will explain what they learned to their classmates.

Evaluation questions:
What did you learn in agriculture?
How do we keep the kitchen safe?
What job did you do for the class job chart?

Summary:
We have learned many useful skills this term. We are proud to show our work.
